title: Bananas, ripe and slightly ripe, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Bananas are the edible fruits of the banana plant (Musa spp.) cultivated in tropical regions worldwide. Raw bananas can be fully ripe or slightly ripe, which influences their taste, texture, and nutrient profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Botanically bananas are berries, although they are commonly called fruits in culinary contexts.
The most widely produced variety is Cavendish, accounting for over 90 % of global production.
Bananas grow in “hands,” each hand containing 10–20 individual fruits.
Raw banana peel is rich in fiber and resistant starch, beneficial for gut microbiota.
Bananas can serve as a natural sweetener in many recipes.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is an antioxidant that supports the immune system.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in amino‑acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Resistant starch in slightly ripe bananas
items.content: Slightly ripe bananas are high in resistant starch, which feeds beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to bananas, especially those with latex‑fruit syndrome.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Consuming large amounts of fully ripe bananas can raise blood glucose levels, which is relevant for people with diabetes.

items.title: Potential pesticide residues
items.content: Bananas are often treated with pesticides; thorough washing before eating is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw bananas can be eaten as a snack, added to smoothies, oatmeal, yogurt, salads, or used in baking. Slightly ripe bananas are excellent for making puree, which can replace eggs in vegan recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bananas at room temperature until they reach the desired ripeness. To slow ripening, place them in the refrigerator; the peel will darken, but the flesh stays fresh for up to 5 days.
